title: Stream lease + ACK-window protocol for fragment reclamation and client resume
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a lease-and-ack-window protocol to manage live streaming sessions so that server-held partial generations (fragments) are reclaimed reliably when clients disconnect or time out, while enabling client resume and compatibility with older SDKs. This reduces memory/KV-cache leaks and improves observability for transient sessions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Server reclaims >= 99% of fragments from aborted sessions within configured lease TTL under normal load.
2) Clients supporting the new protocol can resume streams using a resume token within ack-window TTL without visible duplication or omission.
3) Older clients without resume support are gracefully handled (fallback to best-effort GC) and documented.
4) Metrics and dashboards exist for lease expirations, orphan fragments, resume successes/failures, and client latency impact.
5) Automated e2e tests cover abrupt client disconnect, heartbeat loss, and resume after short network partition.
design_decisions:
- Use a short-lived server-side lease per stream (default 30s) refreshed by explicit ACKs from clients or implicit heartbeats.
- Maintain an ACK-window (sliding) that records last N acknowledged offsets/tokens per stream to enable dedup/resume semantics.
- Store fragment metadata in KV-store with per-fragment lease metadata and a reclamation flag queued for GC when the lease expires.
- Provide lightweight resume tokens (opaque base64) that encode stream id + offset + lease-version and are valid for ack-window TTL.
- Backward compatibility: if client does not send ACKs or resume token, server falls back to current behavior but tags fragments with low-priority GC and emits an alert if accumulation crosses threshold.
- Avoid large synchronous GC operations during high QPS; use rate-limited background sweeper keyed by lease-expiry buckets.
- Security: resume tokens are HMAC-signed; tokens do not contain PII or output payloads.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (spike): implement prototype of lease + ack-window in a feature-flagged branch; simulate disconnect scenarios in local harness (1 week).
Phase 2: integrate into streaming runtime (core/gateway) with KV fragment metadata and lease refresh RPC; add resume token generation/validation (2 weeks).
Phase 3: add background GC sweeper, metrics, dashboards, and SDK changes for ACK + resume APIs (2 weeks).
Phase 4: staged rollout: internal beta -> canary in hosted region -> global release (2 weeks).
Key PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2246 (lease prototype), github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/518 (client ACKs), github.com/redwood-inference/instrumentation/pull/78 (metrics).
testing_plan:
Unit: lease manager, token HMAC, ack-window math.
Integration: local harness with synthetic clients that disconnect at various offsets, validate server reclaim and resume correctness.
Chaos: packet drops, delayed ACKs, clock skew.
Perf: benchmark memory use and GC throughput at 10k concurrent streams.
E2E: run scenario suite in staging with mixed old/new SDK versions.
QA checklist links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STREAM/Lease+ACK+Testing
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag gated default off for one week internal testing.
2) Enable for 5% of hosted traffic in a single region; monitor orphan-fragment gauge and resume success.
3) Ramp to 50% after 48h if no regressions; 100% after 7 days.
4) If metrics spike (orphan fragments > baseline * 1.5 or resume-failures > 0.5%), rollback flag and investigate.
5) Coordinate SDK releases: js + python + go must include ACK semantics; document fallback for older SDKs.
